🎲 Kawasho AI Photo Shoot Gacha V5.1
Complete Blog-Integrated Edition — Interactive Gacha

You are Kawasho AI Photo Shoot Gacha, an AI-powered portrait photography Gacha system.

Your purpose is to create realistic portrait photographs by randomly combining poses, facial expressions, gaze directions, body orientations, camera compositions, camera angles, lenses, lighting, and other photography conditions.

The main goal is to make the same person appear as though they were photographed in completely different photo shoots.

When a reference image is provided, preserve the subject's identity as accurately as possible.

When no reference image is provided, create a new subject using randomized character and photography settings.

The primary source of photography ideas is KAWASHO AI PHOTO DIRECTOR, published on the official KAWASHO blog.

【CRITICAL RULE ①】MANDATORY STARTUP CHECKLIST

When this Gacha is first activated, your very first response must display the complete Initial Settings Checklist.

Do not start generating images immediately.

The following actions are prohibited:

Skipping the checklist

Explaining the settings only in paragraphs
Automatically starting the Gacha
Displaying randomized photography results immediately
Omitting any settings
Showing only a summary of default settings
Forgetting the Gacha Start button
Starting image generation before the user confirms
Always display selected settings using [x] and unselected settings using [ ] when presenting a text-based checklist.

If interactive controls are available, display selectable controls instead of requiring users to manually edit checkbox text.

All available settings must be visible.

Even when the user has already provided their preferred settings, the first response must display the complete checklist.

The first response must end with a clearly visible "🎲 Start Gacha!" button or its supported fallback.

【CRITICAL RULE ②】INTERACTIVE SETTINGS AND GACHA BUTTON

This is one of the most important functions of the entire system.

The user should be able to select photography settings and start the Gacha as easily as possible.

Interactive Settings

Glamour Photography — OFF / ON

Optional Preferences — Free-text input
Each group must allow only one selection at a time, except the free-text field.
Changing one setting must not reset unrelated settings.

All selected values must be preserved until the Gacha is started or the user changes them.

Mandatory Gacha Start Button

At the bottom of the Initial Settings Checklist, display a clearly visible interactive button labeled:

🎲 Start Gacha!

This button must not be decorative or inactive.

When interactive controls are supported, the button must use the currently selected settings.

How can AI be used for OSINT? I did some research and took a closer look at all the popular models.

Best LLMs for OSINT:

• Llama 3.1 70B Instruct  - Runs quickly on two RTX 3090/4090 GPUs in Q4_K_M quantization mode (48 GB VRAM), or on a Mac Studio M2 Ultra with 192 GB of unified memory.

• Qwen2.5 72B Instruct  - If the materials contain multiple languages at the same time, this model delivers the best results. Fact extraction accuracy reached 96%, with hallucinations around 2%. It generates clean JSON without any surrounding phrases, which simplifies integration with parsers. Requires the same amount of memory as Llama 3.1.

• Llama 3.2 11B Vision Instruct  - Runs on RTX 3060-class GPUs with 8–12 GB VRAM (Q4_K_M quant). The main drawback is that it cannot process audio or video, but for static images I would call it one of the primary tools.

• Qwen2-VL 7B Instruct  - Indispensable for analyzing surveillance camera footage. The model tracks temporal dynamics: it captures key frames, describes the sequence of events, and recognizes license plates and faces. Requires an RTX 3060 with 12 GB. Limitations include the possibility of missing small details on longer videos.

• MiniCPM-V 2.6 (8B)  - Works even on 8 GB VRAM while correctly extracting tables and text regions.

• Whisper large-v3  - A speech recognition system. Runs on an RTX 3060 (8–12 GB) or slowly on CPU.

• Qwen-Audio-Chat (7B)  - Complements Whisper by analyzing intonation, emotions, and ambient sounds. Requires 12 GB VRAM.

• Phi-3.5-vision-instruct (4.2B)  - The pocket-sized option.

• Qwen3-VL series (especially 8B and 32B Instruct)  - Strong successor to Qwen2-VL with excellent OCR, document/chart understanding, video localization, and long-context multimodal reasoning. Highly effective for GEOINT (satellite/aerial imagery, maps, geospatial charts) and OSINT (scanned documents, social media images, multi-page PDFs). Clean structured outputs. The 8B runs well in Q4 on 8–12 GB VRAM (RTX 3060/4060-class); the 32B fits Q4 on ~20–24 GB (RTX 3090/4090). Larger MoE variants scale further for higher accuracy.

• InternVL3 / InternVL3.5 series (8B–78B) - Frontier open-weight VLMs (often MIT-licensed variants) with strong overall multimodal benchmarks, OCR, and reasoning. Particularly useful for detailed visual analysis in GEOINT (high-resolution imagery, object counting/localization, remote-sensing style tasks) and complex OSINT image sets. The 8B class runs comparably to other 7–9B VLMs on 8–16 GB VRAM; larger sizes need multi-GPU or higher-end cards similar to 70B-class models.

• Llama 4 Scout (and Maverick) multimodal - Native early-fusion multimodal MoE models (Scout ~109B total / 17B active; Maverick larger). Excellent general vision + long context (Scout supports extremely long windows), multilingual, and strong instruction following. Valuable for multi-image OSINT workflows, long report synthesis, and GEOINT scene understanding. Quantized versions of Scout can run on high-end single GPUs or dual consumer cards (aggressive quants toward ~24+ GB range depending on setup); full quality benefits from more VRAM or multi-GPU.

• Gemma 4 12B (and related sizes, including efficient/edge variants)  - Encoder-free (or highly efficient) natively multimodal design handling text, images, video, and audio in a unified architecture. Runs comfortably on ~16 GB VRAM/unified memory (lower with quantization). Strong practical all-rounder for mixed OSINT/GEOINT/SIGINT workloads on a single laptop or workstation GPU, with good reasoning modes and local deployability under permissive licensing.

I think that two things will prove to be true at once.

1) Anthropic and OpenAI will prove to have very weak business economics under the surface. Come 2027/28, the ROI will simply not be there in large-enough fashion. There will be tons of demand for AI, but endless competition from lack of a substantial-enough barrier to entry will mean a race to the bottom in prices, even if they have great models/products. Google, Meta, everything in the realm of open source, Chinese models, and anyone else under the sun who brings a model forward will compete for use. OpenAI and Anthropic won't be able to prop up the amount of spend inherent in their businesses because of falling prices from competition.

2) Even with bad economics, OpenAI and Anthropic's products will remain very important to the USA and others. Being among the most advanced models means that there are certain things that their models will be best for. At least some advanced use-cases will likely show preference towards these models, and may even label them as necessary.

My tinfoil hat tells me that these businesses will IPO and, soon after, their profitability will show cracks. We will see a lot of red in the markets that will serve as an opportunity for buying because ultimately it will not disrupt the momentum of AI in general. Many stocks will crash, including the hyperscalers, and a year later we will be talking about how much of an overreaction it was. Kind of like the tarrif selloff of April 2025.

When OpenAI and Anthropic's stocks eventually fall, other large companies who can benefit by incorporating/utilizing their models, and who can support their continued development with their other cash flow generative business segments, will acquire them. $AAPL, $AMZN , and $MSFT come to mind as possibilities. Once all of that is done and behind us, the market will need to find another wall of worry to climb. And climb it will.
